chief_complaint: sudden painless dark curtain pulling across vision accompanied by flashes of light and floaters (Retinal Detachment)
hpi_details: 58F highly myopic (nearsighted) woman presents with sudden onset of numerous new black floaters (`like a swarm of gnats`) and bright electrical flashes of light (photopsias) in the temporal visual field of her right eye starting yesterday afternoon. This morning, woke up to find a dark, opaque shadow/curtain spreading from the bottom right corner over her central line of sight, blocking half her right eye vision completely. Zero eye pain or redness.
ideas: terrified that she is going permanently blind in her right eye
concerns: worried because the dark shadow is creeping across the center of her eye right now
expectations: wants emergency retinal evaluation and laser/surgery to reattach her vision
pmh: High Myopia (-8.00 diopters bilaterally), status post uncomplicated cataract surgery right eye 2 years ago

investigation_events.title: Emergency dilated retinal examination
investigation_events.availability_message: The emergency dilated retinal examination is now available. Retina-specialist transfer should proceed immediately.

results.test: Dilated indirect ophthalmoscopy with scleral depression
results.value: Large macula-off rhegmatogenous retinal detachment in the superior-temporal quadrant with a horseshoe tear at 11 o'clock and positive Shafer sign

clinical_knowledge.topic: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes emergency retinal consultation, eye protection, and surgeon-directed positioning while definitive repair is arranged, adapted to the retinal-break configuration and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: sudden painless dark curtain pulling across vision accompanied by flashes of light and floaters (Retinal Detachment)

Key HPI features: 58F highly myopic (nearsighted) woman presents with sudden onset of numerous new black floaters (`like a swarm of gnats`) and bright electrical flashes of light (photopsias) in the temporal visual field of her right eye starting yesterday afternoon. This morning, woke up to find a dark, opaque shadow/curtain spreading from the bottom right corner over her central line of sight, blocking half her right eye vision completely. Zero eye pain or redness.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 76, BP 130/82. External eye exam completely normal without redness (painless white eye). Visual acuity: Right eye 20/200 (down from 20/20 baseline); Left eye 20/20. Confrontation visual field testing demonstrates complete loss of superior and nasal visual fields in the right eye. Relative Afferent Pupillary Defect (RAPD / Marcus Gunn pupil) is POSITIVE in the right eye. Dilated indirect ophthalmoscopy with scleral depression confirms a large, elevated, corrugated, mobile gray-white membrane (detached neurosensory retina) involving the superior temporal quadrant and extending through the macula ('macula-off' retinal detachment), driven by a horseshoe-shaped retinal tear at the 11 o'clock peripheral lattice degeneration site. Shafer sign positive (tobacco dust / pigmented cells floating in anterior vitreous).
Relevant background/PMH: High Myopia (-8.00 diopters bilaterally), status post uncomplicated cataract surgery right eye 2 years ago
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Posterior vitreous detachment (without tear) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Dark curtain/shadow progressing across vision.
management_principles: STAT emergency retinal consultation; protect the eye and follow vitreoretinal-surgeon-directed positioning based on the retinal-break configuration

Urgent transfer to vitreoretinal surgeon for operative repair within 24 hours via Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) with gas/silicone oil tamponade and endolaser retinopexy, OR Scleral Buckle procedure, OR Pneumatic Retinopexy
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 58F highly myopic pseudophakic patient presenting with acute photopsias, shower of floaters, and progressive visual field shadow classic for Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 76, BP 130/82. External eye exam completely normal without redness (painless white eye). Visual acuity: Right eye 20/200 (down from 20/20 baseline); Left eye 20/20. Confrontation visual field testing demonstrates complete loss of superior and nasal visual fields in the right eye. Relative Afferent Pupillary Defect (RAPD / Marcus Gunn pupil) is POSITIVE in the right eye. Dilated indirect ophthalmoscopy with scleral depression confirms a large, elevated, corrugated, mobile gray-white membrane (detached neurosensory retina) involving the superior temporal quadrant and extending through the macula ('macula-off' retinal detachment), driven by a horseshoe-shaped retinal tear at the 11 o'clock peripheral lattice degeneration site. Shafer sign positive (tobacco dust / pigmented cells floating in anterior vitreous).
reference_soap.assessment: Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment of the Right Eye (`Macula-Off` with horseshoe tear at 11 o'clock).
reference_soap.plan: STAT emergency retinal consultation. Protect the eye and follow positioning instructions individualized by the vitreoretinal surgeon to the retinal-break configuration. Urgent transfer for operative repair via pars plana vitrectomy with gas/silicone oil tamponade and endolaser retinopexy, scleral buckle, or pneumatic retinopexy, as clinically appropriate.

learning_objectives: Identify the classic warning symptoms of impending/active Retinal Detachment (photopsias/flashes indicating vitreoretinal traction, acute shower of floaters indicating retinal tear/hemorrhage, and progressive dark curtain shadow)
Correlate predisposing risk factors for rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (high myopia, prior cataract surgery/pseudophakia, lattice degeneration, ocular trauma)

Differentiate the particularly time-sensitive macula-on detachment from macula-off detachment; both require urgent vitreoretinal-surgeon assessment and procedure timing individualized to the clinical findings
Interpret dilated fundus exam findings (corrugated mobile grey retina, horseshoe tears) and Shafer sign (vitreous pigment cells)

teaching.one_liner: 58F highly myopic with sudden floaters, flashes, and a dark curtain spreading across her right visual field, painless.

must_ask.say: Can you describe the shadow? Where did it start, and is it spreading?
Did you notice new floaters or flashes of light before the shadow appeared?
Is there any pain or redness in the eye?

must_ask.objective: Ask about risk factors: myopia and prior eye surgery
must_ask.say: Are you very nearsighted, and have you had any eye surgery like cataract surgery?
This is an emergency. Please protect the eye and follow the retina specialist's individualized positioning instructions during transfer.
